pr_title: arch: arm: cortex_m: Fix meta-IRQ unable to preempt from interrupt
pr_body:
This reverts commit 42036cdbcae270d00b5bd08e805e33bbd3b5787f.

Architecture specific code should not do preemption checking before context switch. This is already handled by the scheduler, so duplicating it would be redundant and error prone. These checks used to be necessary, but the scheduler has been rewritten since then and the checks were removed in 3a0cb2d35d9 (kernel: Remove legacy preemption checking, 2018-05-23).

The added checks tried to address #61761, and were motivated by this in the Architecture Porting Guide:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/5bc6446dcc317d3f3cff49b703ad32e8ecb724cd/doc/hardware/porting/arch.rst?plain=1#L255-L257

However, that part of the guide predates 3a0cb2d35d9 and is outdated. The check was also incorrect, as it didn't take scheduler locking nor meta-IRQs into account, and it was never verified to fix the issue according to [this comment](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761#issuecomment-1946262214).

This PR also updates the meta-IRQ test to verify that meta-IRQs can preempt cooperative threads.

Fixes #80574
pr_comments:
> @kietavainen CI failures seem legit?

@kartben, Yes, the meta-IRQ test is supposed to fail on Cortex-M until #80574 is fixed. This PR just updated an existing test to reveal the issue.

This failure is a regression caused by 42036cd. I'm trying to figure out [here](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761#issuecomment-2621398898) if a revert would be the best way to solve this.
@kietavainen Ah yes, sorry for the noise, I should have read the initial description more carefully
In addition to the test update, this PR is now amended with a fix for #80574.

> This is reverting a fix for another issue.
> 
> As discussed in https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/1334503801402687549

The [PR description](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84509#issue-2809514584) explains why the commit needs to be reverted and that there is no evidence that the commit fixed anything. You also [acknowledged](https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/1334503801402687549/1334513930059649055) that the assumed fix was never tested or verified. So it's just an assumption that the commit contains a fix.

> The documentation in should be updated to:
> 
> > Fetch the cached thread from the ready queue
> > If the ready thread is a metaIRQ or (the current is interruptible and it is different from the current thread), invoke the context switch.
> > Else, do not invoke it.

It's true that the documentation should be updated, but not like that. Instead, it should reflect the current scheduler behavior as explained in 3a0cb2d. I created #84977 to address this.

> The code in this function should be amended as per the suggestion from [#80574 (comment)](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/80574#issuecomment-2451800979)

That's not enough, as that suggestion is still incorrect for scheduler locking. A correct check (albeit redundant as discussed before) is in this [comment](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761#issuecomment-2621398898). I would not like to apply that change as it's redundant and might cause failures in the future if the scheduler is updated. This already happened when meta-IRQs were introduced, and that's what prompted the change to remove these checks from architecture specific code in 3a0cb2d. Besides, it would be adding redundant code into every IRQ.

> You also [acknowledged](https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/1334503801402687549/1334513930059649055) that the assumed fix was never tested or verified. So it's just an assumption that the commit contains a fix.

I acknowledged that no tests had been added to zephyr’s suites, not that is hasn’t been tested at all. @csheaupdesigns were you able to effectively test this? Maybe could you help with adding a test case for your issue?

Considering https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/3a0cb2d35d9499e5f8757bf07260160c448be02e dates back from 2018 and sched.c has had numerous changes since, @andyross is that commit message still relevant? What do you recommend?

> > You also [acknowledged](https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/1334503801402687549/1334513930059649055) that the assumed fix was never tested or verified. So it's just an assumption that the commit contains a fix.
> 
> I acknowledged that no tests had been added to zephyr’s suites, not that is hasn’t been tested at all.

I was referring to this in our Discord conversation:
> > However, it was never verified if the change fixed the issue:
> > https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761#issuecomment-1946262214
>
> Indeed, that is unfortunate 😦

Sorry if I misunderstood it. It would indeed be nice to know how this was tested and verified back then.

> But no reason not to merge this if for no other reason that test coverage over the regression. Which BTW I'm still confused about. Why isn't tests/kernel/sched/preempt catching this? Has anyone looked?

The bug should be triggered if there is a cooperative thread in a busy loop, e.g. `k_busy_wait()`, and then a meta-IRQ thread becomes ready from an IRQ, e.g. correctly timed `k_msleep()`. This is exactly what the meta-IRQ test is doing. I tried to trigger this scenario in the explicit preemption test, but didn't find a clean way yet. There is also this:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/b5c5ba8c832b8ac01b03a8a26ba76a49438b6cc5/tests/kernel/sched/preempt/src/main.c#L90-L97

@ithinuel I take it your "thumbs up" on https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84509#pullrequestreview-2591024822 implies that you're not opposed to this going in? Your "changes requested" review is still blocking the merge however - would you like to dismiss that or change it to "Approved"?
As this fixes a regression introduced in v3.7.0, I'll add the backport labels for v3.7 and v4.0.

issue_context.title: Meta-IRQ does not preempt cooperative threads when woken from IRQ  (cortex_m)
comments:
Hi @Ronvanl! We appreciate you submitting your first issue for our open-source project. 🌟

Even though I'm a bot, I can assure you that the whole community is genuinely grateful for your time and effort. 🤖💙
@wopu-ot Could someone in your team comment here, I assume Meta-IRQ are used by some of your implementations?

Yes, we use Meta-IRQs in our implementation of the controller, but this issue seems to be specific to ARM and therefore does not apply. The test in tests/kernel/sched/metairq tests some of the Meta-IRQ behavior; maybe it could be extended to test for the issue described above.

Hi, [this](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/65071/commits/131ca8a5bee25706926faccb3d126b8cd059d2d5) was introduced as a fix to [#61761](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761).

From [here](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/kernel/services/threads/index.html#meta-irq-priorities):

> […] there is a special subclass of cooperative priorities at the highest (numerically lowest) end of the priority space: meta-IRQ threads. These are scheduled according to their normal priority, but also have the special ability to preempt all other threads (and other meta-IRQ threads) at lower priorities, even if those threads are cooperative and/or have taken a scheduler lock.

and

> Note that because this breaks the promise made to cooperative threads by the Zephyr API (namely that the OS won’t schedule other thread until the current thread deliberately blocks)

@Ronvanl does replacing `(_kernel.cpus->current->base.prio >= 0)` with the following snippet helps ?
```c
((_kernel.cpus->current->base.prio >= 0) || (_kernel.cpus->current->base.prio < (-CONFIG_NUM_COOP_PRIORITIES)))
```

@ithinuel, I replacing the check with the snippet and it doesn't work as it assumes the current thread is a meta-irq thread? Replacing it with the following snippet does work as it checks the cached thread but I am wondering if this check is supposed to be here anyway. I believe the administration is done in `update_cache()`

```
((_kernel.cpus->current->base.prio >= 0) || thread_is_metairq(_kernel.ready_q.cache))
```

Looking at https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761, it doesn't take in account meta-irq threads which according to the documentation (below) can preempt all threads even if they have taken a scheduler lock.

_These are scheduled according to their normal priority, but also have the special ability to preempt all other threads (and other meta-IRQ threads) at lower priorities, even if those threads are cooperative and/or have taken a scheduler lock._

Can we confirm this is a regression and if so will it be fixed and backported to 3.7.0 and if so when?

In the meantime, is there a way to overwrite the z_arm_exc_exit functionfrom application code? We are using workspace application where zephyr is cloned from official repo and we do not have our own fork (yet).

> Can we confirm this is a regression 

I think so yes.

> and if so will it be fixed and backported to 3.7.0

I think it should be backported.

> and if so when?

once a fixed has been proposed & merged.

> In the meantime, is there a way to overwrite the z_arm_exc_exit functionfrom application code? We are using workspace application where zephyr is cloned from official repo and we do not have our own fork (yet).

I don't think so.
Does the snippet you shared in your previous message fix the issue?
If so, I think the fastest would be for you to open a PR with the fix you could validate, ideally with extra tests that would catch future regressions of that feature.

The snippet indeed fixes the issue but I think reverting the changes in [42036cd](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/42036cdbcae270d00b5bd08e805e33bbd3b5787f) should be the way forward however there is a reason why its added right?

There is a sample which demonstrates the constant latency of the meta-irq threads https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/samples/kernel/metairq_dispatch/README.html. Maybe this can be included in the tests with a well-defined criteria

The reason for this change is that it is a fix to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61761.

I don't know if zephyr is able to validate timing accuracy (this highly depends on the simulator/device).
@Ronvanl Would you mind creating a PR with that change you could validate or do you prefer me to create it?
Would appreciate if you could do it, especially if any (unit) testing is required as I'm not familiar with the test framework.

Driving by: scheduler logic really doesn't belong in arch code, and this is a good example why.  It's long since time to migrate cortex-m to arch_switch(), which puts this logic under a z_get_next_switch_handle() API.  I got started in this space a week and a half ago (in the context of "remove PendSV" and not switch/swap per se) and might have something to push soonish.
@andyross I see 3.7.1 is released, any chance a fix is included here already?
Not yet, I'd expect that work at best to be slow-rolled into the default configs.  For this bug we want to address it in the existing code; the comment above was a design nitpick, basically.
An existing test is updated to expose this issue in #84509.
